title: The Daily Five
dek: Five quick questions on today's biggest stories from pole vault history to Champions League heartbreak and basketball transfers.

questions.question: What height did Alex (Aleksandr) Averbukh clear to win Israel's first-ever European Athletics Championships gold, in the pole vault at Munich on 10 August 2002?
questions.explanation: Averbukh won gold in Munich's Olympiastadion by clearing 5.85m; he later set Israel's still-standing national record of 5.93m in 2003.

questions.question: Hapoel Tel Aviv is one of how many candidates pre-accepted to advance to the due-diligence phase of EuroLeague's new 24-team franchise plan?
questions.explanation: Hapoel Tel Aviv was among 11 clubs pre-accepted out of more than 20 initial applicants, while Hapoel Jerusalem missed out.

questions.question: Hapoel Be'er Sheva's Champions League play-off dream ended in Baku after Sabah won the second leg 5-2 in extra time. What was the final aggregate score?
questions.explanation: Sabah overturned a 4-2 aggregate deficit and won 5-2 after extra time to advance 6-4 on aggregate, despite Beer Sheva's 2-1 first-leg win in Beersheba.

questions.question: Maccabi Ashdod completed their five-import roster with forward Markis McDuffie, who has played professionally in Italy, Turkey and France. Which country is he moving to for the first time in his career?
questions.explanation: McDuffie, a Wichita State alumnus, previously played for clubs in Italy, Turkey and France, but this is his first move to Israel.

questions.question: Italian side Lecce made an offer for Hapoel Tel Aviv winger Stav Turiel that the club rejected as too low. How much did Lecce reportedly bid?
questions.explanation: Lecce's roughly €2m offer was turned down; an analyst estimated Hapoel Tel Aviv would need €3-3.5m to sell the 25-year-old, who has no release clause.
